entries.clue: Boy with girlfriend is in French musical party (8)

indicators.note: tells you to translate 'is' into French

blocks.note: GF is the usual short form of girlfriend

annotation.surface: A boy and his girlfriend turn up at a French party with music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In French' seems to say where the party is, but it only turns 'is' into EST.
annotation.definitionFit: A songfest is a gathering where people sing together, a musical party.

entries.clue: First pair of questions in National Curriculum assessment exercises (6)

indicators.note: take the first two letters of 'questions'
one thing sitting in another is surrounded by it, so QU sits inside SATS

blocks.note: SATs are the national tests given in English schools

annotation.surface: A school test whose first two questions are about exercises.
annotation.walkthrough: SATs are the national tests given to children in English schools under the National Curriculum. QU goes in after the S.
annotation.definitionFit: Squats are a common leg exercise.

entries.clue: Fundamental parts in clue edited (6)

indicators.note: an edited text has had its letters changed around

annotation.surface: Someone editing a crossword clue finds its most important parts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word, but it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Nuclei are cores or central parts, the fundamental parts of atoms or cells.

entries.clue: Excellent start, performing in sack (5-4)

indicators.note: letters that are performing are acting out a new arrangement
put the rearranged letters inside FIRE

blocks.note: to sack someone is to fire them
START rearranged, placed after FIR in FIRE

annotation.surface: A great beginning, with a show put on in a sack race.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sack' is a verb here: to fire. FIR + STRAT + E.
annotation.definitionFit: First-rate means of the best quality, excellent.

entries.clue: A lot of sheepdogs flit about showing maximum pace? (5,2,5)

indicators.note: most, but not all, of 'sheepdogs': the last letter goes
the letters are moved about

blocks.note: added to the fodder, 12 letters in all

annotation.surface: Sheepdogs darting around a field at top speed.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: the speed of light is the top speed in physics.
annotation.definitionFit: Nothing can travel faster than the speed of light, so it is the maximum pace.

entries.clue: Endlessly ask and ask for yoga positions (6)

indicators.note: each word loses its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone keeps asking and asking for yoga poses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' applies to all three words, not just the first.
annotation.definitionFit: Asana is the Sanskrit word for a seated or held posture, so yoga positions is a plain translation.

entries.clue: Hackneyed opening in short story (5)

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A tired, clichéd first line in a short story.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short story' reads as one phrase, but 'short' only gives its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Stale ideas or phrases are worn out, hackneyed.

entries.clue: Beat interrupts writers in old clubs (8)

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

blocks.note: nibs are pen points, the parts that write
to lick is to beat, as in 'we licked them'

annotation.surface: A drumbeat breaks in on authors meeting at their old clubs.
annotation.walkthrough: The clubs are golf clubs, not gentlemen's clubs, and 'writers' are pen tips rather than authors.
annotation.definitionFit: A niblick is an old name for a golf club roughly like a nine iron.

entries.clue: Sentimentality of school head avoiding dance (8)

indicators.note: the word's head, its first letter, stays away

blocks.note: SCH is a standard abbreviation of school
head = master, abbreviated M; 'head' is doing double duty

annotation.surface: A school's headteacher staying away from the sentimental school dance.
annotation.walkthrough: The M is the loose spot: solvers at the time read 'head' as master (M) as well as the deletion signal. SCH + M + (W)ALTZ.
annotation.definitionFit: Schmaltz is excessive sentimentality, especially in music or film.

entries.clue: Intermittently, scout in Verdun shot straight (8)

indicators.note: something intermittent comes and goes, so the letters of 'scout' appear only every other place
put the scout letters inside the Verdun letters
something shot is wrecked, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: VERDUN rearranged, split around the inserted letters: UN…RVED
the second and fourth letters of sCoUt

annotation.surface: A scout at the battlefield of Verdun fires a straight shot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot straight' reads as firing accurately, but 'shot' rearranges VERDUN and 'straight' is the definition. UN + CU + RVED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym built by negation: a line without any curve is by definition a straight one.

entries.clue: Has a king’s backing about British stronghold in North Africa (6)

indicators.note: to back is to move backwards, so the letters are read in reverse order
the reversed letters go around B

blocks.note: K is king in chess notation
B is British, as on car stickers

annotation.surface: A king supports a British fort in North Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: HAS A K turned round is KASAH; B goes in the middle: KAS-B-AH.
annotation.definitionFit: A kasbah is the fortified citadel of a North African town.

entries.clue: Bye-bye old Sue’s poorly pets? (4-4,4)

indicators.note: the letters are in a bad way, so they get rearranged

annotation.surface: Saying goodbye to old Sue's sick animals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pets' looks like animals, but here it means favourites, as in teacher's pets. The 's stands for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Blue-eyed boys are favourites who can do no wrong, someone's pets.

entries.clue: Deal with some theatre attendants (5)

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used

annotation.surface: Handling some of the ushers at a theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between the two words, which is where hidden words usually sit.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a book that treats a subject deals with it, and a doctor treats or deals with a patient.

entries.clue: Active old criminal’s hedonistic life (5,4)

indicators.note: criminal letters are bent, so rearranged

annotation.surface: An energetic old crook living a life of pleasure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun, the old crook, but it is an adjective telling you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: La dolce vita, Italian for 'the sweet life', means a life of luxury and pleasure.

entries.clue: Of which a draw ahead of others constitutes a win? (6,6)

definitions.text: Of which a draw ahead of others constitutes a win?

blocks.note: the surface wants a tied game; the setter means being pulled out of a hat

blocks.clueFragment: ahead of others constitutes a win
blocks.note: a draw beating other results sounds like a sporting paradox; in a raffle the first tickets drawn take the prizes

annotation.surface: A game, perhaps chess or football, where a draw beats the other results.
annotation.walkthrough: A draw usually means neither side wins; in a raffle, being drawn before the other tickets is winning.
annotation.definitionFit: Raffle tickets are drawn from a hat, and the first ones drawn win prizes.

entries.clue: Where vigilant Customs official might look, however (2,3,4)

definitions.text: Where vigilant Customs official might look

blocks.clueFragment: Where vigilant Customs official might look
blocks.note: a thorough officer checks every piece of luggage, not just a chosen few
an everyday adverbial phrase meaning 'anyway' or 'be that as it may'

annotation.surface: A customs officer deciding where to search, however.
annotation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: a thorough customs officer might look in any case (suitcase).
annotation.definitionFit: In any case means however, whatever happens.

entries.clue: Juliet’s lot permits supporting better university (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, a support sits underneath

blocks.note: to cap something is to better it

annotation.surface: Juliet's family grants permission that helps a better university.
annotation.walkthrough: LETS goes below CAP + U in the down answer. 'Better' is a verb, not an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: The Capulets are Juliet's family in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet.

entries.clue: On which you’d log who arses about (8)

indicators.note: the letters are moved about

annotation.surface: A diary where you record someone who messes around.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Log' looks like record-keeping; here it means cutting logs. To arse about is British slang for messing around.
annotation.definitionFit: A sawhorse is a frame that holds wood while you saw it into logs.

entries.clue: Annual study period in America mostly decays, unfortunately (8,4)

indicators.note: most of the word: the last letter goes
the letters meet an unlucky jumbling

annotation.surface: A year of study in America goes to ruin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In America' looks like the setting, but AMERICA is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: The academic year is the yearly period of school or university teaching.

entries.clue: Chinese system, one-third Taoism and two-thirds I Ching (3,3)

indicators.note: the first third of the word's letters
the first two-thirds of the letters

blocks.note: the first two of TAOISM's six letters
the first four of ICHING's six letters

annotation.surface: A Chinese philosophy blending Taoism and the I Ching.
annotation.walkthrough: Taoism and the I Ching are both Chinese; the surface stays in the same world as the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Tai chi is a Chinese system of slow exercise and martial art.

entries.clue: One’s boring coat (6)

definitions.note: 'One's boring' describes a person, so it stands for the noun ANORAK

blocks.note: British slang for a dull, obsessive enthusiast

annotation.surface: Someone's dull coat.
annotation.walkthrough: An anorak is British slang for a dull, obsessive enthusiast. 'One's boring' means someone who is boring.
annotation.definitionFit: An anorak is a hooded waterproof jacket, and also a nerdy bore.

entries.clue: Released single? (9)

blocks.note: unfastened, as a horse from a cart
getting hitched is slang for marrying, so an unmarried person has not been

annotation.walkthrough: The second sense is playful: getting hitched is marrying, so someone single is unhitched.
annotation.definitionFit: Unhitched means released from a hitch, as a horse from a cart.

entries.clue: Mean to investigate Guy’s Hospital Trust, initially (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word

annotation.surface: An intention to look into a London hospital trust.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb, intend; it is the adjective, stingy. Guy's is a hospital in London.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for stingy: a tight or mean person hates parting with money.

entries.clue: Long thread about End of Empire (5)

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
'about' can mean around, so YARN wraps around the E

annotation.surface: A long-running story about the end of the Empire, or of Empire magazine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb, to yearn. Empire is italic as the film magazine's title. YARN goes around E: YE-ARN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, but only once 'long' is read as the verb meaning to crave, not the adjective.

entries.clue: Infuriate a Green liberal (6)

indicators.note: letters treated liberally are set free to move

annotation.surface: Annoying a Green who is also a Liberal, a political squabble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Green liberal' looks like a politician; 'liberal' only means freely rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to fill someone with rage or fury.

entries.clue: One wooing Macron upset former queen (8)

indicators.note: letters upset are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: ER = Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth II

annotation.surface: President Macron courting a former queen and upsetting her.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as the French president annoying a queen, but it only rearranges MACRON.
annotation.definitionFit: A romancer is someone who woos or courts.

entries.clue: Tracks onset of sudden change in USA (6)

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: Following an abrupt shift in the United States.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Change' is coins, not alteration. 'Tracks' is a verb: a dog scents its quarry.
annotation.definitionFit: To scent is to track by smell.

entries.clue: * skater is all over the place (8)

indicators.note: the letters are scattered into a new order

annotation.surface: A skater, marked with a star, is sprawling everywhere on the ice.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the symbol itself, printed at the start of the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is the symbol itself rather than a word, a rare trick; its name comes from Greek for 'little star'.
